clauses.reason: Section 1-101 establishes the Federal Legal Council, composed of the Attorney General and representatives of not more than 15 other agencies, each designated by the agency head. Executive Order 13286 section 53 (effective March 1, 2003) struck '15' and inserted '16'. The Council continues as amended. Operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12146 of July 18, 1979 (44 FR 42657; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12146.txt, read in full) establishes the Federal Legal Council (section 1-1), states its functions (1-2), requires a litigation notice system (1-3), directs legal disputes between Executive agencies to the Attorney General (1-4), encourages public availability of legal opinions (1-5), provides for automated legal research and information systems (1-6) and sets agency responsibilities (1-7). Executive Order 12608 section 15 (1987) updated the name of the Department of Health and Human Services and Executive Order 13286 section 53 (2003) raised the member limit from 15 to 16 and added the Department of Homeland Security to the initial list. The two-year initial term of section 1-103 ended the initial-membership roster in 1981. The dossier chain lists Executive Order 12977 for this order but the provision it quotes is the Executive Order 13286 section 53 amendment (the held text of Executive Order 12977 does not mention Executive Order 12146), so it is not treated as an amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
